findings.practical_consequence: A planner still cannot implement the happy-path worktree-safe launch without rediscovery because the candidate requires a launcher-owned trusted Codex hook configuration and authorized fresh-session authentication, but does not ground which trusted config route the launcher can provision or how a fresh CODEX_HOME becomes authenticated without reading or copying credentials.
evidence: candidate-round-2 PO-D1-HOST marks READY while required_inputs still names an authorized authenticated-session provider that can make a fresh per-session Codex home usable without reading or copying credentials.

candidate-round-2 D1 facts state no inspected launcher source creates a governed Codex home, installs hook config, proves trust, runs a challenge, records HostCapabilities, or proves the authorized authenticated-session provider.

EV-D1-OFFICIAL-DISCOVERY grounds Codex hook source/trust categories but does not ground a launcher-installable trusted source route; EV-D1-WRAPPER, EV-D1-EXECUTOR, and EV-D1-TRANSLATOR ground the current absence; EV-D1-HOST only grounds the local verifier after invocation.

findings.practical_consequence: A planner would still have to invent policy facts for the registered-use denominator because the candidate leaves the canonical ineligible_reason_code set and the exact metric numerator/query contract undefined while marking the obligation READY.
evidence: candidate-round-2 PO-D2-ELIGIBILITY required_inputs names a canonical ineligible_reason_code set owned by the telemetry/controller contract, but candidate-round-2 D2-FUTURE-ELIGIBILITY lists a planner obligation to define those values instead of supplying them.

candidate-round-2 D2-FUTURE-ELIGIBILITY defines registered_dispatches as eligible intents with a selected registered/successor dispatch according to the implemented dispatch policy, which is not an exact planner-ready durable query contract.

EV-D2-EVENTS, EV-D2-CONTROLLER, EV-D2-REGISTRY, and EV-D2-SELECTOR ground the current absence of eligibility and denominator facts; EV-D3-CONTRACT grounds that owner contracts currently lack recurrence_policy and availability_policy.

findings.practical_consequence: A planner cannot produce a one-shot implementation plan for the owner registry because the candidate supplies source paths, hashes, and fail-closed states, but not the concrete per-owner parameter schemas, canonical calls, budgets, effects, reconciliation rules, terminal schemas, or recurrence values that the requirement asks the research package to make implementation-ready.
evidence: candidate-round-2 D3-CURRENT-OWNER-CONTRACTS reports materialized_field_counts of 0 for parameter_schema, canonical_argv_or_typed_call, action_class, full_unit_budget, effect_identity, reconciliation, terminal_schema, recurrence_policy, availability_policy, and implementation_source_hash_in_registry.

candidate-round-2 owner_rows provide implementation_source and sha256 for available/helper rows, but do not extract the executable constants needed to build the materialized contracts without rereading those sources.

candidate-round-2 PO-D3-OWNER-CONTRACTS marks READY while its closure condition still requires resolving every row to executable constants or fail-closed state; EV-D3-MANIFEST, EV-D3-CONTRACT, EV-D3-DESCRIPTORS, and EV-D3-SEQUENCES each explicitly limit descriptor/catalog/identifier evidence as non-executable.
